commands.description: The project as the Objects panel lists it. `plates`: each `{index, name, objects}`, with the objects that have an instance on it, each time with that plate's instances; `outside`: those with an instance on no plate. An object has `index`, `id`, `name`, `filament`, `part_count`, `size` (mm, of its bbox), `instances`, the indices of its instances there, and `instance_ids`, their ids in the same order. With `detail` it also has `auto_drop`, `bbox` (instance 0), `brim_ears` (a count), `overrides` (the keys of the settings it overrides, which `settings_get` target object reads), `mesh_errors` as the list's warning icon reads them (`open_edges`, manifold, and the loader's or a repair's `degenerate_facets`, `edges_fixed`, `facets_removed`, `facets_reversed` and `backwards_edges`; `object_fix` repairs them), `instances` as entries (`index`, `id`, `offset`, `rotation_deg`, `scale`, `mirrored`, `bbox`), and `parts`: parts, negative parts, modifiers, support blockers and enforcers and precise seams, each with `id`, `type` (`subtype` for a precise seam), `filament` (a part's own or its object's, a modifier's only when it sets one), `position`, `bbox` and `scaled_volume` (mm3) on the bed for instance 0, `rotation_deg` and `scale` in the object's frame, `mirrored`, `triangles`, `mesh_volume` (the unscaled mesh's mm3), `painted` facets (supports, seam enforcers/blockers, `fuzzy_skin`, mmu per filament, texture per layer), and a text part's text and font or an SVG part's file. When it has them: `layer_config_ranges`, its height range modifiers (`[{min_z, max_z, values}]`, for `object_set_height_ranges` and `settings_set` target `height_range`), and `layer_height_profile` (`{points, min_height, max_height}`). commands.description:
Read the settings named: each item has its `value`, as OrcaSlicer writes it, and `meta`: `label`, `description` (what the setting does, when to change it), `where` (its settings page and group), `type`, `unit`, range, allowed values and `mode`. Keys the settings lack go to `unknown_keys`, with `type_of` (where each is a setting: a type, or project) and `similar` (keys like the others). It needs `keys`, `compare` or a `target` other than global; `settings_list` lists a type's settings, a page at a time with `where`.
- No `type`: `keys` are looked up in the process, filament and printer settings, and each item names its type, the one `settings_set` takes.
- Target global: the preset being edited, or a saved `preset`; `compare` lists only the keys that differ (`value` and `other`). A per-variant value's `meta` has `variants` (what each entry is for) and `active` (the entry each extruder prints with).
- Target object, part or `height_range`: without `keys`, what it overrides; with them, the process settings it takes (`settings_list` type object or region) and extruder, its filament; a key it does not take is refused with where it is set. Each item has `value` (its own, or null), `effective` (what it prints with) and `source`, the first of `height_range`, part, object, global or default to set it. An object's item lists in `parts` the parts and modifiers that override the key in their volume, and an object's or part's in `height_ranges` the ranges that apply to it. In a modifier (mesh or painted) that sets none of a key, the overlapped part's value applies, which is not worked out: where a part or an earlier modifier sets the key, the modifier's item has `effective` null, `source` `overlapped_part`, `object_effective` and `object_source`, and in `parts` those that set it. The reply names the target.
`preferences_get` reads the app's preferences, `plate_get_settings` a plate's settings and `project_get_settings` the project's own.

preset.description: Read this saved preset of the type (a name from `preset_list`) instead of the one being edited.

commands.title: Read settings

commands.description:
Change settings as typing them into their settings tab would: a type's preset (target global, the default), or the overrides of an object, a part or a height range. Values are strings in OrcaSlicer's format ("15%", "0.2", "1,2") or JSON numbers, booleans and arrays (a point as `[x, y]`). All are parsed strictly first and applied together, so nothing changes if one is invalid; a key of another type is refused with that type named. Reply: `applied`, and `changed`, every setting the call changed, including those the app adjusted in turn. An object's or part's change is one undo step; a preset's is not in the undo history. Spiral vase and a few others confirm their adjustments in a dialog (`blocked_by_dialog`).
- Target global: a null value takes a key back to its saved value, or with `reset_to` parent to the parent's; `reset_all` first discards every unsaved change, as the tab's undo button does (reply: `reverted`). A per-variant value (`settings_get` `meta.variants`) takes one value for the entries in use (`meta.active`), `{index, value}` for one entry, or an array of all.
- Type printer: `extruders_count` goes alone, as the Printer settings' Extruders field sets it; `nozzle_volume_type` sets each extruder's nozzle flow type as its sidebar card does. A `nozzle_diameter` of another variant of the printer model selects that variant's preset, as the sidebar's nozzle diameter does, with only `nozzle_volume_type` beside it (other keys go in a second call); a flow type the new preset's nozzle card does not offer is refused with those it does. The switch asks about the printer's unsaved changes (`blocked_by_dialog`) unless `reset_all` discards them first, which stays if the switch is not made.
- Target object, part or `height_range`: overrides of the keys its row offers in Prepare (`settings_list` type object or region), and `extruder`; a key it does not take is refused with where it is set. null removes one; a height range keeps its `layer_height`, checked against the printer's layer heights for the range's filament. `extruder` is the target's filament (1-based; 0 or null for Default, the object's), set as the Change Filament menu does. The reply names the target.
`plate_set_settings` changes a plate's settings and `project_set_settings` the project's own. `preferences_set` changes the app's preferences; those it refuses (`preferences_get` marks them) change in the Preferences dialog: `window_open {"window": "preferences", "tab": "<tab>", "key": "<key>"}`, then `widget_set_value {"target": {"name": "<key>", "within": "Preferences"}, "value": ...}`.

part.description: Part index in the object (target part, with object); without both, the part selected in Prepare.

reset_all.description: Target global: discard the unsaved changes before applying values.

reset_to.description: Target global: what a null value takes a key back to: the saved preset (default) or the preset it inherits from.

target.description: Where they apply: global (default), the type's preset; object, part or `height_range`, the overrides an object, one of its parts or modifiers, or one of its height ranges carries, which are process settings.

type.description: Which settings: the printer, process or filament preset being edited.

commands.description: Delete a filament slot, as its Delete menu item does, the objects on it taking the first filament; with `merge_into`, as its Merge with item does, the objects on it taking that slot. The slots after it move down by one. A mixed filament (`filament_list`'s mixed rows) is deleted as the mixed filament list deletes it, and not merged. A physical filament that a mixed filament mixes is deleted as the sidebar deletes it: the mix is broken (`broken_mixed`) until `filament_edit_mixed` names its filaments again. A merge into a mixed filament that mixes the slot asks first, as Merge with does, and replies `blocked_by_dialog`, unless `break_mix` answers: `true` merges, `false` refuses (`mixed_uses_slot`). A physical slot before a later one on a non-Bambu Lab printer with more than one nozzle and without `single_extruder_multi_material` asks before the later slots' tool numbers shift, and replies `blocked_by_dialog`, unless `confirm_shift` answers: `true` deletes, `false` refuses (`shifts_tools`); a cancel is refused (`delete_cancelled`). The slots are independent of the printer's extruders, so a toolchanger deletes them too. Refused: the only physical slot, and a mixed filament while one physical slot is left, where the sidebar hides the mixed filaments (`filament_add` first). Not in the undo history. Reply: `filament_slot` (the slot deleted), `merged_into` (the slot its objects went to, as numbered afterwards), `filament_slots`, and `broken_mixed` (the mixed filaments broken afterwards, as numbered then) where there are any.

With neither components nor ratios it opens the Add Mixed Filament dialog, as the sidebar's button does, and replies `blocked_by_dialog`. commands.description: Install printer models, for good, as ticking them in the Printer Selection dialog and pressing Confirm does: a vendor's profiles are installed from the ones OrcaSlicer ships, the presets reloaded, and a printer newly added selected. The other installed models are kept, and the installed filaments but for what the reload changes. A name no model has, a vendor or a nozzle a model lacks, is refused with the closest names. Reloading the presets drops their unsaved changes, so while there are some `preset_changes` says what becomes of them; without it the call is refused. A call that changes nothing reloads nothing. Mesh and matrix arrays need numpy, which `script_list_api` says is installed or not; a file run's PEP 723 block can install it. The code runs on a worker thread, where calls documented as UI thread only raise RuntimeError. The run ends once its code and the non-daemon threads and pool tasks it started are done; its windows close with it. `args` holds the args you pass; set `result` to a JSON value to return it; print() output comes back as output. Reply: `{status: finished | raised | cancelled | timed_out, result, output, traceback?, message?}`; a script that raised changed what it changed before. The code's own file access is held to OrcaSlicer's folders (its data folder, and read only its resources folder and, for a file run, the file's folder), and it starts no programs or threads and reaches no network: such an access raises PermissionError, unless a person has let Python scripts run unrestricted in Preferences (`app_state.python.scripts_unrestricted`), when the threads and pool tasks it starts call the tools too while the run lasts; the tools it calls work as they do for you. Recorded by `replay_export` as one step with its code, which a replay runs again against the project as it is then.

commands.description: Record a video of OrcaSlicer until `recording_stop`: MJPEG frames with their real timestamps in a Matroska (.mkv) file. Captions show the tool call acting on the app at the bottom (secret setting values never show); pointer highlights the pointer, its clicks rippling. Capture takes at most about a third of the UI thread, so the frame rate drops where capturing is slow. One recording at a time: a replay's or script's ends with it, a client's when the server is turned off. With encode, the `recording_stop` that reports it also writes an MP4 beside it and deletes the .mkv unless `keep_raw_video_file`; `recording_encode` encodes any recording later. With no arguments it opens the Start Recording dialog (`blocked_by_dialog`), whose controls are named after their settings for `widget_set_value`; its "Start recording" starts the person's recording, which neither a replay's or script's end nor the server turning off ends, and the dialog remembers the settings. `silent: true` starts one at once with the defaults.

commands.description: Stop the running recording. Call it with `silent: true` for the report: it waits for the file and returns it with its seconds, frames captured and written, frames dropped when encoding fell behind, failed when they could not be encoded, or skipped when the window could not be captured, the size, the mean UI-thread time a capture took (`capture_ms`), and why it ended. A recording that ended on its own (`max_seconds`, the replay or script that started it ended, a write error) is reported once by the next `recording_stop`. For a recording started with encode, it then starts the MP4 encode and returns it under encode: a job, whose `app_wait {for: "job"}` returns `recording_encode`'s result, whose `raw_video_file_deleted` says whether the .mkv was deleted. Called with no arguments, it stops the recording as Stop Recording does, whoever started it: without waiting for its file, it shows the person a notification naming it and replies with its path; the next `recording_stop` with `silent: true` reports it as ended `stopped_in_app`.

commands.description: Select a body, a face, edges, a vertex, a reference plane, a sketch's loop or a feature by id, as a click selects it. One form: body; body with face, edges (the last the current edge, as in a Shift+click set) or vertex; plane; sketch with loop; feature; or nothing, which clears the selection. A body is selected as a click on its row of the Bodies list selects it, a face, edges or a vertex as a click in the view picks them, a loop as a click on it, which also selects its Sketch's row, and a feature as a click on its row of the Feature list. A plane is picked only where a click can pick one: while the Origin row shows the planes, or while Sketch waits for its plane (sketch_create {}), where picking it opens the sketch. A loop is numbered as sketch_describe {sketch} numbers closed_loops and solid_extrude {sketch, loop} takes it, and is selected only while the view shows it: an extrude that takes the whole sketch hides the sketch, and one that takes a loop hides that loop. Whatever was selected goes first, of every kind. The menu-item forms then act on the selection: feature_edit, design_rename_selected, feature_delete and sketch_constrain_selected called with no arguments act on the selected row of the Feature list while nothing is picked in the view, and design_zoom_to_selection acts on what is picked in the view, so a sketch is zoomed to through sketch with loop, not through feature. Refused, changing nothing, for an id the model does not have, and while a card, a sketch, Constrain mode, a body Move or the Text dialog is open, where a click means something else. Reply: selection {kind, id}, plane and feature, as design_describe reports selection, picked_plane and feature_row; for a vertex also point, as body_describe gives it, and placed_point, where the view draws it (the same unless the body was moved).

commands.description: Confirm what is open in the Design tab, as its Confirm button and Enter do. What is open, in the order Confirm takes it: the Text dialog (text), a value field (value), a body Move (move), a text or art placement (insert), a feature card (card), a sketch (sketch), Constrain mode (constrain). The Text dialog takes it as its OK does: a new text goes into the design, its placement then open (insert), and an edited one keeps its new words. A card adds or edits its feature in one undo step and closes; an add the card refuses, or whose rebuild fails, leaves no feature and no undo step and keeps the card open with the reason on the status line. A Confirm that does not take, such as that add or a value that is no number, replies ok false. It runs under what is open, which refuses the commands that change the document. commands.description: Draw a shape in the open sketch from its fields beside `type`, or a list of shapes as `entities`. Each type, and the fields it takes: line {p0, p1}; polyline {points: 2 or more, a loop when the last is the first}; rectangle_2_point {p0, p1: opposite corners}; rectangle_center {center, corner}; rectangle_3_point {p0, p1: one side; width: signed, to the left of p0 to p1}; rectangle_rounded {p0, p1: opposite corners; radius: of the corners}; circle_center {center, radius}; circle_2_point {p0, p1: the ends of a diameter}; circle_3_point {p0, p1, p2: on the circle}; arc_3_point {p0: start; p1: end; on_arc}; arc_center {center, radius, start_angle, end_angle}; arc_tangent {end; entity: the line or arc it leaves, the sketch's or one an item before it adds, at that one's end, along its direction there, left out the one added last}; slot {c0, c1, width}; slot_arc {center, start, end: its direction from the centre, width}; ellipse {center, radius (semi-major), rminor, rotation}; ellipse_arc {the ellipse's fields, start_angle, end_angle: parametric, counter-clockwise}; spline {ctrl: 2 or more poles}; polygon {center, sides, radius (to a vertex) or across_flats, angle (of that vertex, or of the first edge's midpoint)}; point {p}. A type refuses a field it does not take. Each is built as its drawing tool builds it: a rectangle, a slot or a polygon is one shape, which one undo of the sketch takes off whole, and a polyline is its lines, as its tool leaves them; the constraints are inferred exactly, so that none moves what is given. Each shape carries the constraints its tool gives it, at any slant; a constraint between a shape and the sketch's axes or what is already in the sketch, or between plain lines, is inferred only where it holds exactly, so a square on the axes is level only on a side lying exactly on one, with right angles holding the others. Each item of entities may carry its own construction; the top-level construction is the single-type form's, and beside entities each item's that gives none. Beside entities a shape's field, type among them, is refused: it belongs in its item. Points are [x, y] in the sketch plane (mm); angles are radians, or degrees as start_angle_deg and the like. A polygon is lines; its side count is not kept once committed. Reply: first_index, added, shapes [{first, count}] per item, entities, dof. Called with exactly one of these argument sets and nothing else, it opens that item's tool of the Design tab for a person, as the menu item does: {"type":"line"} (Line), {"type":"polyline"} (Polyline), {"type":"rectangle_2_point"} (Corner rectangle), {"type":"rectangle_center"} (Center rectangle), {"type":"rectangle_3_point"} (Oblique rectangle), {"type":"rectangle_rounded"} (Rounded rectangle), {"type":"circle_center"} (Center circle), {"type":"circle_2_point"} (2-point circle), {"type":"circle_3_point"} (3-point circle), {"type":"arc_3_point"} (3-point arc), {"type":"arc_tangent"} (Tangent arc), {"type":"arc_center"} (Center-point arc), {"type":"slot"} (Slot), {"type":"slot_arc"} (Arc slot), {"type":"ellipse"} (Ellipse), {"type":"ellipse_arc"} (Elliptical arc), {"type":"spline"} (Spline), {"sides":3,"type":"polygon"} (Triangle), {"sides":4,"type":"polygon"} (Square), {"sides":5,"type":"polygon"} (Pentagon), {"sides":6,"type":"polygon"} (Hexagon), {"sides":8,"type":"polygon"} (Octagon), {"sides":12,"type":"polygon"} (Dodecagon), {"type":"point"} (Point).

Describe what is on screen as an indented tree, one element per line with a ref for `widget_click`, `widget_set_value`, `keyboard_press`, `webview_run_javascript` and, for a page element, `mouse_gesture`: every shown window's widgets, the rows of lists, trees and tables, each shown popup after the window it opened from, the main menus, the 3D canvas's toolbar items and gizmos, each ImGui panel of the last frame with its items and text, and each shown web page's elements (dialogs, the setup wizard, sign-in, plugin windows). With a modal dialog open, only the topmost dialog's pages are read. A ref goes stale when its element goes away; list again then. Prefer `action_run` and the typed tools when one fits.
A locator names an element without a ref, in any session (`replay_export` records them); index (0-based) picks one of several matches:
- a widget: `{label, class, name, within, index}`, within being its window's title; a notebook page: `{tab: "General", within}`
- a setting's field: `{option: "layer_height"}`
- `{menu: "File>Export>Export G-code"}`, `{gltoolbar: "arrange"}`, `{gizmo: "Move"}`
- an ImGui item: `{imgui: "label", imgui_name?: "name", window?, canvas?, index?}`, by label, name or both
- a row of a list, tree, table or drop-down list: `{row: "Plate 1>Cube>Cylinder", column?, within?, index?}`, by its last labels; column names the cell to act on
- a plate or its icon in Prepare: `{plate_icon: "lock", plate: 0}`: plate, delete, orient, arrange, lock, settings, name, `move_to_front`, `filament_map` or `imex_mode`
- a web page's element: `{web: "Next", kind?: "button", css?: "#AcceptBtn", within?, index?}`, by its listed label (exact, else any case, else a part), kind, CSS selector (a line's name=#save is `{css: "#save"}`), or together. Without within it looks in the topmost dialog's pages while one is open, else in every shown page; an action waits for its element up to 2 s short of `timeout_s` (default 8 s), but at least 3 s or all of a shorter `timeout_s`.

commands.description:
Click a GUI element as a person would. A plain left click activates menu items, buttons, checkboxes, toggles, radio buttons, toolbar items and gizmos as their owners expect (a menu item takes any click, a toolbar item a right one too); with modifiers, double or another button a control gets a mouse click, which a native one ignores. A gizmo opens and a second click closes it (Text on an object without text creates a text part: created). Other widgets and ImGui items get a mouse click once scrolled into view, at x/y (logical pixels from the top left) on a 3D canvas or custom-drawn widget; modifiers reach the 3D canvas, the object list and handlers that read them. A row is selected as a click on its cell selects it (ctrl adds, shift extends; in the object list the named column acts, as Printable toggles), double activates it and a right click opens its menu; a drop-down list's row is picked. A plate icon does what it does in Prepare: lock replies locked, arrange and orient reply done once their job ends, settings and `filament_map` list the dialog they open (dialogs). To click a point of the model, drag, scroll or hold a press, use `mouse_gesture`. A menu the click opens is never shown: the reply lists it as `popup_menu`, or `popup_item` runs one of its items (ran). A click that opens a dialog replies `blocked_by_dialog`.
A web page's element gets a click's pointer and mouse events at its centre (or x/y) once scrolled into view, refused when something covers that point. The reply reads back checked, and has closed when the click closed its dialog (with dialogs, those still open under it, which need an answer), navigated (with url) when it changed the page, or dialogs when it opened another. Otherwise page says what changed within 300 ms: changed (false when its lines are as before), the `widget_list` lines added and removed, partial when a plugin configuration frame could not be compared, and posted, how many messages the page sent OrcaSlicer.

commands.description:
Make a mouse gesture on a 3D canvas as a person would: move, down, up, click, drag or wheel. It starts at `at`, a model point projected through the camera and by default checked to land on that part, or at x/y, logical pixels from the canvas's top left. A drag goes through `waypoints` to `to`: on an object it moves the object; in a painting gizmo, from a press on the object being painted, it paints (a zigzag over an area paints all of it); elsewhere it turns or pans the camera as this install's mouse settings say, so turn the camera with `view_set` instead. A wheel turns delta notches: positive zooms in (out with the Reverse mouse zoom preference) or scrolls a panel up. Modifiers are held as keys for the gesture (shift picks points in Measure and erases in a painting gizmo). A down keeps its button and modifiers held, so moves drag, until an up or another gesture. Grabbers are set through the gizmo's panel fields or `object_transform`, not dragged. A menu a right click opens is listed as `popup_menu`, or `popup_item` (with click or up) runs one of its items. `camera_moved` in the reply says the camera moved, so earlier screenshots and pixels no longer match.
With target, the gesture is on a web page's element instead (a canvas such as the colour picker's spectrum, a slider, a sortable or scrolled list): x/y, to and waypoints are logical pixels from its top left, a drag keeps the pointer captured where the page asks, and a wheel scrolls what is under the pointer unless the page takes it; page says what changed, as for `widget_click`.

at.description: A point of the model: object, instance and part (default 0), and point `[x, y, z]` in the part's mesh coordinates (frame part) or the scene's (frame world), or spot, where a ray along that axis first meets the part.

canvas.description: Default current, the view shown. design takes x/y only.

check.description: For model points: check they land on the part (surface, default) or only project them (point).

delta.description: Wheel notches (default 1 on a canvas; a page element needs it given).

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the input: ctrl and cmd are Command on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere; rawctrl is the macOS Control key.

popup_item.description: The item to run of a menu the input opens (a context menu, a button's menu), by label path ("Add Modifier>Cylinder"; "#2": a repeated label's second). Without it the reply lists the menu (`popup_menu`) instead of showing it.

target.description: A web page's element (its ref or a `{web}`/`{css}` locator) to gesture on instead of a 3D canvas.

timeout_s.description: For a web page's element: seconds the page gets to answer (default 10).

to.description: A canvas pixel `[x, y]` or a point of the model, as for at.

tolerance.description: Surface check distance in mm (default 1% of the part's size, at least 0.1).

waypoints.description: Where a drag goes after the start, before to.

items.description: A canvas pixel `[x, y]` or a point of the model, as for at.

commands.description: Press a button of the topmost modal dialog: yes, no, ok, cancel, close, apply, a button's label, or a numeric id. A disabled button (`enabled: false`) is refused, the dialog's message showing what it still needs, and so is one on a page the dialog does not show, except a hidden cancel or close, which ends the dialog. On a dialog that is neither native nor a web dialog, a standard name or id it has no button for ends it with that answer too, without a handler running (`pressed: false`). The label of an option of a selector made of buttons (Orca's radio groups, tab bars and multi-switches, shown as (*) / ( ) in the message) selects that option and leaves the dialog open; set other radio buttons and switches with `widget_click` or `widget_set_value` true, and notebook tabs with `widget_click`. dialog.title, text the dialog's title contains, makes sure which dialog that is; it must be the topmost. Reply: dialog, button, pressed, and id, the wx id pressed or ended with, or `web: true` for a button on a web dialog's page, with what the page did as `widget_click` reports it; `closed: true` when it closed, and dialogs, those still open. A native message box (`native: true`) is pressed through the OS, by one of the buttons `app_state.dialogs` lists for it; a file or folder picker can't be answered here, nor any native dialog on macOS (its buttons list is empty): register `dialog_auto_answer` before opening them. A web dialog's buttons are on its page: a label is pressed there, waiting up to 3 s for it to show, so the page's own handler runs. With no such page button, or a page busy for those 3 s, cancel and close end the dialog, and ok, yes, no and apply are refused rather than skip the page's commit; `page_buttons` then lists the page's buttons.
commands.title: Answer a dialog

commands.description: Answer modal dialogs automatically when their title or message matches a rule's regex (case-insensitive). `app_state.auto_answer_rules` lists the rules in force. Called from a replay or script, the rules join those it set before and last until it ends, and a plugin's likewise until it unloads or loses its permission to call the tools; an MCP client's replace the ones MCP clients set before and last until the MCP server stops, and an empty list clears them. Reply: scope (run, plugin or session), rules (uses counts a rule's answers) and `answered_open_dialog`. A native dialog returns the rule's button at once and never shows. A file or folder picker takes button ok with an absolute path and returns it without showing; without a path a picker can only be cancelled, and a multi-select picker takes no path. A wx dialog is answered as `dialog_answer` does. A matching dialog already open is answered too (`answered_open_dialog`), so a prompt that shows around the same time, such as the restore prompt after startup, is caught either way. A web dialog is matched by its title: a button that names one of its shown wx buttons (by label, standard name or id) is pressed as for a wx dialog, any other on its page once it shows there, for up to 10 s after the page loads; past that, cancel and close end the dialog and any other button gives up.

button.description: yes | no | ok | cancel | close | apply | label | id

match.description: Regex searched in "title\nmessage", in "title\ntext" (the dialog's own static text, one line each, without its controls), and in the title alone for a dialog with no text (a web dialog), so ^Title$ matches it.

overwrite.description: A save picker may return an existing file at path (default false).

path.description: Absolute path a matching file or folder picker returns, with button ok. A picker has no title until it shows, so the rule matches its prompt and must not anchor on a title with ^. The rule answers pickers only: an open picker needs an existing file, a folder picker an existing folder, and a save picker the file's final name, new unless overwrite: overwrite is checked against this path, and the picker's caller may still add an extension. A picker the path can't serve is cancelled and the reason logged.

commands.description: Evaluate JavaScript in one of OrcaSlicer's web views (Home, the device page, dialogs, plugin windows). Prefer `widget_list` and the input tools (`widget_click`, `widget_set_value`, `keyboard_press`, `mouse_gesture`), which see and drive pages as they do widgets. The code runs in the target's page: a web view's (kind webview in `widget_list`), or a page element's, with the element as `el`; without a target, in the topmost dialog's web view, else in the only shown one. While a modal dialog is open, only its pages run code. Reply: result, the value of the last expression (JSON values come back parsed), and url; `closed: true` when the code closed its dialog, `navigated: true` when it changed the page, dialogs when it opened another. Messages the page posts to OrcaSlicer reach it once the code has returned. It runs through eval, which a page whose Content-Security-Policy forbids it may refuse (`widget_list` and the input tools still work there).

code.description: JavaScript statements, run through eval: the last expression's value is the result. No top-level return or await; a Promise or a DOM node comes back as {}.

target.description: A web view (its ref; `widget_list` lists it as kind webview) or an element of its page (its ref or a `{web}` / `{css}` locator), which the code gets as `el`. Default: the topmost dialog's web view, else the only one shown.
